turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in, the chair by the desk is grand. What brought you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor I'm really worried. It's the cramps and the bloating, my bowels are all over the shop.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ok. How long has this been going on, and what actually happens?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): A year, um, a full year. Some days I'm bunged up for ages and then it goes loose, the cramp eases once I pass a stool, and the stress in work sets the cramp off. Is that serious? Be honest with me.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): So, playing that back, cramps that ease when you open the bowels, bloating, and the stool alternating between constipation and loose, for a year.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes that's it. And the stress in work is making it worse. Could it be cancer? I need you to tell me.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): I won't dodge it, we'll get there. Any blood in the stool, red or black?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None. I check every time.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you lost weight without trying?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No weight loss. The jeans are tighter but that's the bloat, not weight.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I take buscapan as well, 10 milligrams when the cramp hits, usually twice a day. Is that making the loose stools? Should I stop it?
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Unlikely to be the cause of a whole year of this. Stay on the 10 milligrams for the cramps for now. Anything else you're taking?
[SEG0013] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Err, the nurse wrote sertraline fifty milligrams on the sheet this morning. Once a day, she said.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah no, that's not right. I'm on a hundred milligrams every morning. She has the old dose. It's for the anxiety, I've had the anxiety for years.

[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, two different doses on the table and I won't pick one. We'll check it with the chemist. The anxiety we know about. Tell me the family history, since you were fretting about cancer.

[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, my brother is grand, and another sister has pressure but no sugar. No bowel cancer in the family, not that I know of anyway.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Father with the diabetes, your sister with pressure, and your mother did not have it. Day to day now, the job, the hours, what you eat, the exercise and the drink?

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): I work in the accounts office in the county council, 37 hours a week, mostly stuck at the desk. The diet is sandwiches and tea, I don't get any exercise, I don't walk or anything, and I'll have a glass of wine most nights and two glasses at the weekend.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me have a feel of the tummy. Soft, tender low on the left, no lumps that I can find.

[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): With that pattern over the year, the cramp settling after you go, no blood and no weight loss, my working impression is irritable bowel. I still can't rule out coeliac or some inflammation until the bloods are back.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): So not cancer? Will the bloods show if it is? When are they, I can't wait months, I'm not able for the worry.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nothing in the story screams cancer. Bloods won't prove or disprove a growth. I'll book them this week, full blood count, coeliac screen and a crp.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): And a scan? Please can I have a scan. I read about it online and I can't let it go.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): We might do a scan if it does not settle. I'm not arranging one today.
[SEG0025] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She'll only half hear the food advice, she's that wound up. Can you say it plain?

[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Smaller meals, a bit more fibre, ease off the white bread and the fizzy drinks, and keep the wine to a couple of nights rather than most nights. That's for you to try yourself.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): If I do all that does it actually settle? Do I come back? And what if I'm worse at the weekend, do I go to the hospital?
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let's see you in two weeks with the results. If you pass blood, or you can't keep fluids down, then you go to the hospital.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. Ok. Umm, and the hundred milligrams, you're sure that's not wrecking the bowel?
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): I don't think the sertraline is behind this, whatever the dose turns out to be. You were right to come in.

spec.situation: Person with cramps relieved by passing stool, bloating, alternating constipation and loose stools for a year; stress at work; denies blood and weight loss after prompting; bloods planned, diet advice.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

omissions.text: Sertraline dose as stated by the patient was 100 mg every morning; the recorded medication entry only says once daily and misses the patient's stated dose.
Negative family history of bowel cancer: patient said there was no bowel cancer in the family as far as they knew.
Brother is well/'grand' with no relevant illness reported.
Doctor advised that blood tests will not prove or disprove a growth/cancer.
